name: Girgaon Chowpatty
description: Mumbai's premier and most iconic immersion venue. On Anant Chaturdashi (Day 10), millions line Marine Drive as grand historic idols—including Lalbaugcha Raja, Mumbaicha Raja, and Chinchpoklicha Chintamani—arrive with massive Dhol-Tasha pathaks for their grand Arabian Sea immersion.
nearestStations: Charni Road (Western Line) - direct footbridge access to beach
processionRoute: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marg ➔ Byculla ➔ Two Tanks ➔ Opera House ➔ Girgaon Chowpatty
peakDays: Anant Chaturdashi (Day 10 - All night until dawn)
bmcFacilities: BMC Medical Emergency tents & Ambulance bay
Free high-capacity mobile drinking water tankers
trafficAdvisory: Marine Drive and Dr. B.A. Road are fully closed to private vehicular traffic. Local trains run 24 hours continuously on Western Railway with special night services.
tideSafetyTip: Strictly heed Mumbai Fire Brigade siren warnings. Never attempt to wade beyond designated safe barricades due to strong tidal undertows.

name: Juhu Beach
description: The cultural epicenter for immersion in Mumbai's Western Suburbs. Famed for vibrant coastal aarti processions, celebrity idol immersions, and thousands of eco-friendly community celebrations stretching across the wide sandy beach.
processionRoute: Swami Vivekananda Rd ➔ Juhu Tara Road ➔ Shivaji Statue ➔ Juhu Beach entry
trafficAdvisory: Juhu Tara Road operates one-way toward the beach. Parking is prohibited within 1 km of beach entrances.
tideSafetyTip: Beware of stingrays and jellyfish during evening high tide. Beach volunteers provide rubber boots at medical booths if needed.

name: Dadar Chowpatty & Chaityabhoomi
description: Located directly facing the Bandra-Worli Sea Link and adjoining historic Shivaji Park. This historic South-Central Mumbai beach hosts reverent immersions from the cultural heartland of Dadar, Mahim, and Prabhadevi.
nearestStations: Dadar Railway Station (Major Central & Western Junction)
processionRoute: Ranade Road ➔ Senapati Bapat Marg ➔ Cadell Road ➔ Chaityabhoomi entrance
bmcFacilities: Large-scale mobile crane immersion assistance for heavy idols
trafficAdvisory: Dadar Station is within 12 minutes walking distance. Cadell Road is restricted to immersion procession vehicles only.
tideSafetyTip: Rocky shoreline near sea link—stay on designated sand tracks marked by police barricades.

name: Versova Beach
description: Steeped in authentic coastal Koli fishing heritage. Versova Beach is world-famous as the immersion destination for Andhericha Raja, whose legendary 21-hour procession arrives on Sankashti Chaturthi (5 days after Anant Chaturdashi) escorted by decorated traditional fishing trawlers.
processionRoute: Veera Desai Road ➔ J.P. Road ➔ Seven Bungalows ➔ Versova Beach
peakDays: Sankashti Chaturthi (Day 15/16 - Andhericha Raja Grand Immersion)
bmcFacilities: Koli fishing boat escorts deep into the sea
Artificial tank zones for Shadu clay idols
trafficAdvisory: Best accessed via Mumbai Metro Line 1 (Versova Station). Avoid driving as fishing village lanes are narrow.
tideSafetyTip: High surf during mid-September tides. Only authorized Koli fishermen operate boats into deep water.

name: Powai Lake (Ganesh Ghat)
description: The premier inland immersion venue in Mumbai's eastern and central suburban corridors. Surrounded by scenic hills and green boulevards, featuring state-of-the-art eco-immersion tanks to protect lake ecology.
majorPandals: Sahyadri Krida Mandal (Tilak Nagar - Eco Immersion)
processionRoute: Adi Shankaracharya Marg ➔ JVLR ➔ Ganesh Ghat Promenade
bmcFacilities: Special idol cranes for large suburban mandals
trafficAdvisory: JVLR traffic remains busy. Use public transit or drop-off points near Hiranandani.
tideSafetyTip: Freshwater lake—no sea tides, but steep shoreline drop-offs. Immersions restricted to paved ghats.
